turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip, the threat was real and not just from the Mussulmans. Nikhil's people were suffering under Sandip's oppression, and he could not idly stand by while Sandip continued to destabilize their land.
turns.speech: I warn you, Sandip, the threat is real and not just from the Mussulmans. My people are suffering under your oppression, and I cannot idly stand by while you continue to destabilize our land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was well aware of the suffering Nikhil referred to. However, Sandip insisted that it was he who possessed the power to bring about true change, not Nikhil with his outdated methods.
turns.speech: Oh, Nikhil, do not think I am unaware of the suffering you speak of. But let me remind you, it is I who holds the power to bring about true change, not you with your outdated ways.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his methods, while capable of bringing change, also led to oppression and suffering. He insisted that he could no longer stand by and watch his people endure such hardship, and demanded that Sandip leave his territory.
turns.speech: Your methods may bring change, but they bring oppression and suffering as well. I will not stand by and watch my people suffer any longer. You must leave my territory.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that his methods, though noble, were also naive. Sandip insisted that he brought fire and passion to the cause, not the cold logic of a man who feared change. However, Sandip assured Nikhil that he would leave his territory as requested, for he knew when to choose his battles.
turns.speech: My dear Nikhil, your methods may be noble, but they are also naive. I bring fire and passion to the cause, not the cold logic of a man who fears change. But do not worry, I shall leave your territory as you request, for I know when to choose my battles.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's departure was welcome, but do not think that his concern for his people and his land was mere fear. He acted out of principle and responsibility.
turns.speech: Your departure is welcome, but do not think that my concern for my people and my land is mere fear. I act out of principle and responsibility.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala was torn between the two of them, each with their own convictions and ways of seeing the world. She wished to understand both sides but feared the consequences of choosing one over the other.
turns.speech: I am torn between the two of you, each with your own convictions and ways of seeing the world. I wish to understand both sides but fear the consequences of choosing one over the other.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip understood Nikhil's principles, but he reminded Nikhil that principles were like the wind; they could change direction with a single breath of passion. And Bimala, he told her, do not fear the choices she must make. Every choice was a step forward, whether it led her to the sun or the shadows.
turns.speech: I understand your principles, Nikhil, but remember that principles are like the wind; they can change direction with a single breath of passion. And Bimala, do not fear the choices you must make. Every choice is a step forward, whether it leads you to the sun or the shadows.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala saw both points. But how could she choose between the passion that Sandip offered and the responsibility that Nikhil upheld? Each path held its own truth.
turns.speech: I see your points, both of you. But how can I choose between the passion that Sandip offers and the responsibility that Nikhil upholds? Each path holds its own truth.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's dear Bimala must see that Sandip's path is a dangerous one. It may bring excitement and change, but it also brings instability and suffering. Choose the path of duty and reason.
turns.speech: My dear Bimala, you must see that Sandip's path is a dangerous one. It may bring excitement and change, but it also brings instability and suffering. Choose the path of duty and reason.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala saw the truth in both Nikhil and Sandip's words. Yet, how could she decide without feeling the full weight of her heart's pull?
turns.speech: I see the truth in both your words, Nikhil and Sandip. Yet, how can I decide without feeling the full weight of my heart's pull?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil understood Bimala's confusion, but he told her that she must not let her heart be swayed by Sandip's rhetoric. His words may sound appealing, but they lead to chaos and strife. He urged her to see the clear path of duty and stability.
turns.speech: I understand your confusion, Bimala, but you must not let your heart be swayed by Sandip's rhetoric. His words may sound appealing, but they lead to chaos and strife. I urge you to see the clear path of duty and stability.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he was speaking of duty and stability, but where was the soul in that? The heart of the country beat with passion, not just duty. Bimala, a mirror to the nation, yearned for the light of truth and freedom, not the shadows of submission.
turns.speech: My dear Nikhil, you speak of duty and stability, but where is the soul in that? The heart of this country beats with passion, not just duty. Bimala, you are a mirror to the nation, and like you, it yearns for the light of truth and freedom, not the shadows of submission.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala was torn, truly. Sandip spoke of the soul and truth, but Nikhil warned of the dangers that lay ahead. How could she choose when both seemed so right, yet so wrong?
turns.speech: I am torn, truly. Sandip speaks of the soul and truth, but Nikhil warns of the dangers that lie ahead. How can I choose when both seem so right, yet so wrong?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: How could a woman of Bimala's spirit be content with shadows when the sun of truth beckoned? Nikhil spoke of duty, but he forgot the fire that burned within each of them, urging them to break free from the chains of oppression.
turns.speech: How can a woman of Bimala's spirit be content with shadows when the sun of truth beckons? Nikhil speaks of duty, but he forgets the fire that burns within each of us, urging us to break free from the chains of oppression.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala felt the fire in her heart as Sandip spoke, yet Nikhil's words of caution resonated within her. How could she reconcile her longing for truth with the fear of chaos?
turns.speech: I feel the fire in my heart as Sandip says, yet Nikhil's words of caution resonate within me. How can I reconcile my longing for truth with the fear of chaos?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip spoke of duty, but he asked Nikhil to what end. To a system that chains people and stifles their dreams? No, Bimala, the path she must choose is the one that leads to the liberation of their souls. It was not in shadows but in the light of truth that they found their strength.
turns.speech: Nikhil, you speak of duty, but duty to what? To a system that chains our people and stifles their dreams? No, Bimala, the path you must choose is the one that leads to the liberation of our souls. It is not in shadows but in the light of truth that we find our strength.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala was lost, caught between the light of truth and the shadows of fear. Sandip spoke of fire and freedom, yet Nikhil warned of the dangers that lurked. How could she choose when both paths called to her heart?
turns.speech: I am lost, caught between the light of truth and the shadows of fear. Sandip, you speak of fire and freedom, yet Nikhil warns of the dangers that lurk. How can I choose when both paths call to my heart?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip again. He told Sandip that his words might inspire, but his actions brought peril. Nikhil insisted that Sandip cease his schemes against Nikhil's people or face the consequences.
turns.speech: I warn you again, Sandip. Your words may inspire, but your actions bring peril. Cease your schemes against my people or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip asked Nikhil about the shadows he had mentioned, questioning if they were not of Nikhil's own creation. Sandip pointed out that while Nikhil warned of danger, he, Sandip, saw only the oppressive chains of a system that suffocated the people. Sandip insisted that it was their duty to break these chains rather than submit to them.
turns.speech: And what of the shadows you speak of, Nikhil? Are they not of your own making? You warn of danger, but I see only the chains of a system that stifles the very breath of our people. Is it not our duty to break these chains, not to bow to them?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala was torn, for she saw the fire in Sandip's eyes and the shadows in Nikhil's words. Yet, how could she choose when both spoke to pieces of her heart?
turns.speech: I am torn, for I see the fire in Sandip's eyes and the shadows in Nikhil's words. Yet, how can I choose when both speak to pieces of my heart?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would flee, Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was just telling Queen Bee about their college club and the contest over the translation of lines from Browning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that he managed to translate the lines into Bengali but doubted it would be a joy forever for the people of Bengal, and recalled old Dakshina's rendering, adding that Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the warning was about the fever fit of poesy.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up local Mussulmans and that they might attack Sandip any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and suggested that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he did not offer advice and wished Sandip would refrain from giving him advice, and that he must ask Sandip to leave his territory due to the worrying and oppression of his tenantry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the threat was for fear of the Mussulmans or if there was another fear.
